## Sheet W1 — Heo Thần Thoại (pig_thienlong): idle → WINDUP → attack

- Lưu thành: `art_inbox/.batch/rig-02-windup/W1.png`
- Đính kèm (theo thứ tự): `1_style_creature.png`, `W1_2_hint.png`, `W1_3_hint.png`, `W1_4_hint.png`
- Kết quả: lưới 1×3: cal_pig_thienlong_idle, cb_pig_thienlong_windup, cal_pig_thienlong_attack

```text
Image 1 is the STYLE REFERENCE: finished art from my game. Copy its art style exactly: a dark warm-brown outline (never black) of even weight, soft cel shading with one shadow tone and one highlight tone, light from the top-left, warm pastel colours of medium saturation, a subtle painted texture, rounded chunky friendly shapes, low-to-medium detail. Do NOT copy the objects of image 1.
Image 2 is the accepted look of this exact creature (Heo Thần Thoại) standing in its IDLE pose: match its shape, colours and shading closely, but leave out any text or letters.
Image 3 is the accepted look of the same creature in its ATTACK pose, lunging to the right: match its shape, colours and shading closely, but leave out any text or letters.
Image 4 only shows the SHAPE idea for the layout of the three cells: one creature per cell, same size, feet on the ground line at the bottom, the body upright in cell 1, crouched low and pulled back to the left in cell 2, stretched forward to the right in cell 3. Ignore its style completely (its heavy outline, glossy look, cloud pedestal and captions are wrong for my game).

Draw ONE image: a sheet of 3 separate game sprites in a clean grid of 1 row(s) x 3 column(s), in exactly this order, left to right, top to bottom:
Row 1: (1) IDLE pose — the same pose as image 2, standing ready on all four legs; (2) WINDUP pose — the moment just BEFORE the pounce of cell 3: crouched low and coiled like a spring, the weight sitting back on the bent hind legs, the body leaning back to the LEFT, front legs bent under the chest, head lowered and pulled in, both wings raised high and swept back ready to beat, tail curled tight, the same determined frown as image 3, eyes fixed on the right; (3) ATTACK pose — the same pose as image 3, lunging forward to the right in mid-pounce.
All three cells show the SAME single creature: Heo Thần Thoại, the creature shown in images 2 and 3. Keep it IDENTICAL to images 2 and 3: the same colours, markings, crown, cape, jewels, wings and body proportions, drawn at the SAME scale as in images 2 and 3.
The three cells are three moments of ONE attack, read left to right: ready, wind up, strike. Cell 2 is the new drawing; it must look like it belongs between cells 1 and 3. EVERY pose faces RIGHT (three-quarter view looking to the right). It is a cute hero creature.
A character pose sheet: each cell holds the whole creature once, at the SAME size in every cell, its feet resting on the same invisible ground line at the bottom of the cell, about 80 % of the cell height tall (a crouch is lower, a lunge is wider, but never outside the cell). Expressive cartoon acting, clear silhouette. No props, effects, motion lines, dust, stars or text around it.

Every object is fully visible and centred in its own cell, with wide empty gaps between objects; nothing touches, overlaps or crosses into another cell. Wide landscape image.
Background: one plain flat light-grey colour (#C8C8C8) everywhere. No gradient, no texture, no floor, no cast shadow on the background.
No text, letters, numbers, labels, captions, watermark, logo, border or frame. Not glossy, not a 3D render, not flat vector, not pixel art. No glow, no sparkles, no floating particles.
```
